issues.legal_issue: Whether the status of land as part of an owner’s reserved or selected area is a jurisdictional fact in a tenant’s application to purchase the land.
material_facts: A tenant applied to purchase land that he had cultivated for more than six years.
The landowner initially asserted that the land was reserved, and later contended in revision that it had been selected as part of the permissible area.
The authorities below allowed the purchase application without resolving whether the land had been validly selected.
issues.conclusion: Whether the land was part of the reserved or selected area was a jurisdictional fact. The Financial Commissioner had revisional jurisdiction to examine whether the authorities below had rightly assumed jurisdiction to deal with the purchase application.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 18(1) and 18(2) of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, a tenant may purchase only eligible land, and the Assistant Collector must address the land’s eligibility before determining its value. An erroneous decision on that threshold fact cannot confer jurisdiction. Under section 24 of that Act read with section 84 of the Tenancy Act, the Financial Commissioner’s revisional power permits review of whether subordinate authorities rightly assumed jurisdiction. Chaube Jagdish Prasad v. Chaturvedi and Jagannath Ramchandra Datar v. Dattaraya Balwant Hingmire were followed; Rai Brij Raj Krishna v. S.K. Shaw, Queen v. Commissioners for Special Purposes of Income Tax, and Colonial Bank of Australia v. Willan were held inapplicable.

rule.if: tenant_purchase_proceeding and land_exclusion_status_disputed and subordinate_authority_allowed_purchase and revision_challenges_assumed_jurisdiction

predicates.tenant_purchase_proceeding: A tenant seeks to purchase land held under a tenancy.
predicates.land_exclusion_status_disputed: A party disputes whether the land falls within an area that makes it ineligible for purchase.
predicates.subordinate_authority_allowed_purchase: A subordinate authority allows the purchase application or proceeds to determine the purchase price.
predicates.revision_challenges_assumed_jurisdiction: A party seeks revision on the ground that the subordinate authority lacked jurisdiction because of the land’s exclusion status.

issues.definition: When a tenant’s purchase proceeding involves a dispute over the land’s exclusion status and revision challenges the subordinate authority’s jurisdiction, the revisional authority must review whether that jurisdiction was rightly assumed.
